title: Jeremiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 40 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 40.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 40, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard lets Jeremiah go from Ramah
Jeremiah goes to Gedaliah at Mizpah
The captain of the guard loosens Jeremiah from his chains
Jeremiah is told to dwell with Gedaliah among the people
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard lets Jeremiah go from Ramah
questions.explanation: This event is described first in Jeremiah 40:1, before the other events.

questions.question: Who let Jeremiah go from Ramah?
options: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
Gedaliah son of Ahikam
The king of Babylon
Ahikam son of Shaphan
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:1 states that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let Jeremiah go from Ramah.

questions.question: What did the captain of the guard say the LORD had pronounced upon this place?
options: This evil
Blessing and peace
Prosperity and growth
Freedom and safety
questions.correctAnswer: This evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:2 records that the captain of the guard said, "The LORD thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place."

questions.question: Why did the LORD bring the evil upon the place according to Jeremiah 40?
options: Because they have sinned against the LORD and not obeyed His voice
Because they were strong and prosperous
Because they were faithful and humble
Because they sought the LORD with all their heart
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have sinned against the LORD and not obeyed His voice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:3 explains that the LORD brought this upon them because they sinned and did not obey His voice.

questions.question: What offer did the captain of the guard make to Jeremiah regarding going to Babylon?
options: If it seems good to come with me to Babylon, come; if not, go wherever you choose
You must come to Babylon without choice
Stay here and do not leave
Go to Egypt if you want
questions.correctAnswer: If it seems good to come with me to Babylon, come; if not, go wherever you choose
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4 states the captain's offer that Jeremiah may come to Babylon or go wherever he thinks best.

questions.question: What did the captain of the guard do for Jeremiah before letting him go?
options: Gave him victuals and a reward
Imprisoned him again
Sent him directly to Babylon
Ignored him completely
questions.correctAnswer: Gave him victuals and a reward
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5 says the captain gave Jeremiah food and a reward before letting him go.

questions.question: To whom was Jeremiah instructed to go and dwell with among the people?
options: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
The king of Babylon
Ahikam the son of Shaphan
questions.correctAnswer: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5 directs Jeremiah to go to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam and dwell with him among the people.

questions.question: Where did Jeremiah go to meet Gedaliah?
options: Mizpah
Babylon
Ramah
Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:6 states that Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah.

questions.question: Who had the king of Babylon made governor over the cities of Judah?
options: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
Jeremiah the prophet
Ahikam the son of Shaphan
questions.correctAnswer: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5 says the king of Babylon made Gedaliah governor over the cities of Judah.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's condition when Nebuzaradan took him from Ramah?
options: Bound in chains
Free and unbound
Hidden in a cave
Riding a horse
questions.correctAnswer: Bound in chains
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:1 describes Jeremiah as being bound in chains when Nebuzaradan took him.

questions.question: The captain of the guard told Jeremiah he was free from what?
options: The chains upon his hand
His duty to the king
His captivity in Babylon
His prophetic mission
questions.correctAnswer: The chains upon his hand
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4 states the captain of the guard loosened Jeremiah from the chains on his hand.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was released from captivity to go wherever he deemed convenient.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4 and 40:5 show Jeremiah was allowed to go wherever he thought good and convenient.

questions.question: True or False: Gedaliah was the son of Ahikam, who was the son of Shaphan.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5 explicitly states Gedaliah is the son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

questions.question: True or False: The captain of the guard imprisoned Jeremiah again after releasing him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4-5 shows the captain of the guard released Jeremiah and gave him supplies; there is no mention of re-imprisonment.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was taken directly to Babylon after being loosened from his chains.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4-6 indicate Jeremiah was given a choice and eventually went to Mizpah to dwell with Gedaliah, not directly to Babylon.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 40 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did the king of Babylon make governor in the land according to Jeremiah 40:7?
options: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
Ishmael the son of Nethaniah
Johanan the son of Kareah
Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth
questions.correctAnswer: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:7 states that the king of Babylon made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 40:9 promise will happen if the people serve the king of Babylon as commanded in Jeremiah 40:8?
options: It shall be well with you
You will be taken captive
You will be prosperous in all things
You will be free from all enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be well with you
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:9 says that if they serve the Chaldeans and the king of Babylon, 'it shall be well with you,' which follows the command to serve the king in verse 8.

questions.question: What did Gedaliah instruct the people to do with their wine, summer fruits, and oil according to Jeremiah 40:10?
options: Gather and put them in their vessels
Destroy them to prevent enemies from taking them
Sell them to the Babylonians
Eat and drink them immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Gather and put them in their vessels
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:10 instructs the people to gather wine, summer fruits, and oil and put them in their vessels.

questions.question: How are the Jews described in Jeremiah 40:12 in relation to the news in Jeremiah 40:11?
options: They returned from all places to the land of Judah
They fled further to Moab and Ammon
They rebelled against Gedaliah
They were scattered and did not return
questions.correctAnswer: They returned from all places to the land of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:12 connects with verse 11 by showing that because the Jews heard about Gedaliah's appointment, they returned from all places to Judah.

questions.question: What does the appointment of Gedaliah as governor teach about trusting God’s providence during difficult times?
options: God can use political leaders to bring peace
All leaders are untrustworthy
God abandons His people in captivity
Peace depends only on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: God can use political leaders to bring peace
questions.explanation: Gedaliah’s appointment as governor by Babylon shows that God’s providence can work through political leaders to maintain peace among His people (Jeremiah 40:7).

questions.question: How does Gedaliah encourage the people to live after their captivity according to Jeremiah 40:9-10?
options: Fear not, serve the king, dwell in your cities
Escape to other countries
Rebel against the Chaldeans
Live in hiding without working
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not, serve the king, dwell in your cities
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:9-10 shows Gedaliah encouraging the people not to fear, to serve the king of Babylon, and to dwell in their cities.

questions.question: What practical advice does Gedaliah give regarding provisions for the coming times in Jeremiah 40:10?
options: Gather wine, summer fruits, and oil and store them
Sell all your provisions to Babylon
Give away your food to the poor
Stop farming and wait for help
questions.correctAnswer: Gather wine, summer fruits, and oil and store them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:10 advises the people to gather and store wine, summer fruits, and oil in their vessels.

questions.question: What does the return of the Jews from various countries to Judah demonstrate about their response to Gedaliah’s leadership according to Jeremiah 40:11-12?
options: They trusted his leadership and wanted to live under him
They wanted to rebel against Babylon
They were forced to return by Babylonian soldiers
They were fleeing from famine
questions.correctAnswer: They trusted his leadership and wanted to live under him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:11-12 shows that hearing about Gedaliah’s appointment encouraged the Jews to return, indicating trust in his leadership.

questions.question: How can believers today apply Gedaliah’s instruction to 'fear not to serve' in Jeremiah 40:9 to their own lives?
options: By trusting God and obeying authorities even in difficult circumstances
By avoiding all worldly governments
By expecting immediate deliverance from trials
By ignoring authority and relying on self
questions.correctAnswer: By trusting God and obeying authorities even in difficult circumstances
questions.explanation: Gedaliah’s counsel not to fear but serve the king encourages believers to trust God and obey authorities despite hardships (Jeremiah 40:9).

questions.question: What lesson about community restoration can be drawn from the Jews gathering food and returning home in Jeremiah 40:12?
options: Rebuilding community requires faith and practical preparation
Restoration happens without effort
Isolation is preferable after trauma
Returning home is always dangerous
questions.correctAnswer: Rebuilding community requires faith and practical preparation
questions.explanation: The gathering of food and the return of Jews in Jeremiah 40:12 illustrate that restoration requires both trust and practical action.

questions.question: Why was Gedaliah’s oath to the captains and their men important for peace as seen in Jeremiah 40:9?
options: It reassured them not to fear and to serve Babylon
It threatened them with punishment
It demanded total obedience without question
It commanded immediate rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: It reassured them not to fear and to serve Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:9 shows Gedaliah swearing to the captains not to fear but to serve the king of Babylon, promoting peace and order.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah’s choice to dwell with Gedaliah among the people show about Christian conduct in times of uncertainty (Jeremiah 40:6)?
options: Faithful presence and solidarity with the community
Avoidance of difficult situations
Seeking personal safety only
Rejection of authority
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful presence and solidarity with the community
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:6 demonstrates his choice to stay faithfully with Gedaliah and the people, showing solidarity despite uncertainty.

questions.question: How does Gedaliah’s decision to dwell at Mizpah to serve the Chaldeans reflect a principle of leadership in Jeremiah 40:10?
options: Leaders serve alongside their people
Leaders isolate themselves from the people
Leaders avoid responsibility
Leaders act independently of authority
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders serve alongside their people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:10 shows Gedaliah choosing to dwell at Mizpah to serve the Chaldeans, illustrating servant leadership.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was released from chains and given the choice to go to Babylon or stay in the land according to Jeremiah 40:4.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4 clearly states that Jeremiah was freed from chains and given the choice to go to Babylon or stay where he wished.

questions.question: True or False: Gedaliah ordered the people to abandon their cities and live only in Mizpah according to Jeremiah 40:10.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:10 instructs people to dwell in their cities, not abandon them and live only in Mizpah.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 40.

questions.question: Who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah along with all the captains of the forces that were in the fields?
options: Johanan the son of Kareah
Ishmael the son of Nethaniah
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
Jonathan the son of Kareah
questions.correctAnswer: Johanan the son of Kareah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:13 states, 'Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields, came to Gedaliah to Mizpah.'

questions.question: What warning did Johanan and the captains bring to Gedaliah regarding Baalis, king of the Ammonites?
options: That Baalis sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay Gedaliah
That Nebuzaradan was coming to capture Gedaliah
That the Chaldeans planned to exile all remaining Jews
That Johanan himself was going to betray Gedaliah
questions.correctAnswer: That Baalis sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay Gedaliah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:14 reports, 'Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites hath sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee?'

questions.question: How did Gedaliah respond to the warning about Ishmael's plot?
options: He believed them not
He immediately fled Mizpah
He sent soldiers to arrest Ishmael
He called a council to discuss the threat
questions.correctAnswer: He believed them not
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:14 states, 'But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not.'

questions.question: What did Johanan secretly request from Gedaliah concerning Ishmael?
options: Permission to kill Ishmael without anyone knowing
Permission to flee to Egypt
To make peace with Ishmael
To send Ishmael to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Permission to kill Ishmael without anyone knowing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:15 reads, 'Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it.'

questions.question: Why did Johanan argue that Ishmael should be slain?
options: Because if Ishmael killed Gedaliah, the Jews gathered would scatter and perish
Because Ishmael had stolen supplies from Mizpah
Because Ishmael supported the Chaldeans
Because Ishmael was a traitor to the Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: Because if Ishmael killed Gedaliah, the Jews gathered would scatter and perish
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:15 explains, 'Wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?'

questions.question: What reason did Gedaliah give for refusing Johanan's request to kill Ishmael?
options: Because Johanan was speaking falsely of Ishmael
Because he trusted Ishmael completely
Because he feared causing a civil war
Because he was under Babylonian orders
questions.correctAnswer: Because Johanan was speaking falsely of Ishmael
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:16 states, 'Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Nethaniah' (as in Ishmael the son of Nethaniah) in Jeremiah 40:14 mean?
options: Given of the LORD
Servant of God
God has given
Gift of Yahweh
questions.correctAnswer: Given of the LORD
questions.explanation: The Hebrew name 'Nethaniah' (נתניה) means 'Given of the LORD,' as found in Jeremiah 40:14 where Ishmael is called the son of Nethaniah.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 40:13-16, illustrating the tension between trust and suspicion?
options: Dramatic irony
Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Dramatic irony
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:13-16 uses dramatic irony where the audience knows the danger Ishmael poses, but Gedaliah does not believe the warnings, creating tension.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament echoes the theme of trusting God's appointed leaders despite threats, as seen in Jeremiah 40:9?
options: Romans 13:1-2
Acts 5:29
Hebrews 13:17
1 Timothy 3:1-7
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 13:1-2
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1-2 emphasizes submitting to governing authorities, paralleling Jeremiah 40:9 where Gedaliah urges the people to serve the king of Babylon.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the theme of a remnant being preserved after judgment, as reflected in Jeremiah 40:12?
options: Isaiah 10:20-22
Exodus 12:37
Deuteronomy 7:6
1 Kings 19:18
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 10:20-22
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:20-22 speaks of a remnant of Israel returning after judgment, connecting with Jeremiah 40:12 where Jews return to Judah to Gedaliah.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the arrival of Johanan and the captains to Gedaliah in Mizpah?
options: All the Jews who were dispersed returned to Judah
Jeremiah was released from captivity
Gedaliah was appointed governor by the king of Babylon
The Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: All the Jews who were dispersed returned to Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:11-12 describe how Jews from Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other lands returned to Judah to Gedaliah before the captains came in verse 13.

questions.question: In the context of Jeremiah 40, what does the name 'Gedaliah' mean, and how does it typologically relate to his role?
options: Yahweh is great; he serves as a type of God's appointed governor
Servant of God; he typifies the suffering servant
God is my judge; he foreshadows divine judgment
Peace of God; he symbolizes the coming Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: Yahweh is great; he serves as a type of God's appointed governor
questions.explanation: The name 'Gedaliah' means 'Yahweh is great' and he typifies God's appointed leadership over remnant Israel after exile, as seen in Jeremiah 40:5-7.

questions.question: How does Gedaliah’s refusal to let Johanan kill Ishmael reflect a literary device or theological theme common in prophetic literature?
options: Theme of false accusation and innocence
Theme of retribution and justice
Use of allegory for Israel’s restoration
Paradox of divine sovereignty and human agency
questions.correctAnswer: Theme of false accusation and innocence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:16 shows Gedaliah rejecting Johanan's claim as false, reflecting the prophetic theme of defending innocence against false accusations.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word in Jeremiah 40:9 conveys the concept of 'fear not' and is often used to encourage courage in prophetic texts?
options: אַל־תִּירָא (Al-tira)
חָשַׁב (Chashav)
שָׁלַם (Shalam)
רָפָא (Rafa)
questions.correctAnswer: אַל־תִּירָא (Al-tira)
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 40:9, Gedaliah says 'Fear not' using the Hebrew phrase 'אַל־תִּירָא (Al-tira)', a common prophetic exhortation to courage.

questions.question: True or False: Gedaliah accepted Johanan’s plan to kill Ishmael secretly to prevent the scattering of the Jews.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:16 clearly states that Gedaliah refused Johanan’s request and said it was a false accusation against Ishmael.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 40 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 40:3 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Sin leads to certain divine judgment as a consequence of disobedience
God ignores human sin if repentance is absent
Divine judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions
Human sin can postpone God's judgment indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to certain divine judgment as a consequence of disobedience
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:3 states that the LORD has done what He said because the people sinned and did not obey, showing judgment is a direct result of sin and disobedience.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providential sovereignty is taught in Jeremiah 40:1 regarding Jeremiah's release?
options: God sovereignly directs events even through foreign rulers to accomplish His purposes
God is limited and unable to influence foreign captains
God acts only through Israelite leaders to fulfill His will
Human free will overrides divine sovereignty in captivity situations
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs events even through foreign rulers to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:1 shows that Jeremiah’s release by Nebuzaradan, a Babylonian captain, occurs under the word from the LORD, demonstrating God's sovereign control over foreign powers.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine mercy and human responsibility is taught in Jeremiah 40:4?
options: God grants freedom of choice even after judgment, holding humans accountable
God forces all people to submit to His will without choice
Divine mercy removes all consequences of sin automatically
Human choice is irrelevant once God has judged
questions.correctAnswer: God grants freedom of choice even after judgment, holding humans accountable
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 40:4, the captain offers Jeremiah freedom to choose whether to go to Babylon or stay, showing God’s mercy includes allowing human responsibility and decision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 40:3 specifically demonstrate?
options: Holiness
Omnipotence
Immutability
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:3 reflects God's holiness in that He judges sin and punishes disobedience, demonstrating His moral purity and justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 40:1 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Jealousy
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:1 shows God’s sovereignty as He directs the release of Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian captain, demonstrating control over nations.

questions.question: How does the chapter Jeremiah 40 prepare for the theme of restoration and covenant faithfulness in later Scripture?
options: By showing God’s preservation of a remnant to rebuild after judgment
By depicting total destruction without hope of restoration
By emphasizing complete exile with no return
By focusing solely on punishment without covenant implications
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God’s preservation of a remnant to rebuild after judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:6-12 describes those remaining in the land under Gedaliah, highlighting God’s faithfulness in preserving a remnant to continue His covenant promises.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Jeremiah 40:9-10 have with New Testament teachings on submission to governing authorities?
options: It prefigures the New Testament call to submit to earthly authorities as ordained by God
It rejects any cooperation with foreign rulers as sinful
It promotes violent rebellion against oppressive governments
It teaches that God's kingdom excludes earthly governance
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the New Testament call to submit to earthly authorities as ordained by God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:9-10 encourages the people to serve the king of Babylon, foreshadowing New Testament principles such as Romans 13:1 about submitting to governing authorities.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 40:3 and 40:9 teach about divine judgment and human response?
options: God judges sin but calls His people to faithful submission even under judgment
God’s judgment nullifies all future human responsibility
Human obedience can prevent divine judgment once pronounced
Divine judgment excludes any call to continued service
questions.correctAnswer: God judges sin but calls His people to faithful submission even under judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:3 reveals God's judgment for sin; 40:9 shows Gedaliah urging people to serve the Babylonian king, indicating submission after judgment is required.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 40:4 and 40:5 teach about human freedom and divine providence?
options: God’s providence allows for human choice within His sovereign plan
Human freedom is an illusion under divine providence
Divine providence removes all human responsibility
God forces all decisions regardless of human will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence allows for human choice within His sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:4-5 show Jeremiah’s freedom to choose his path, yet this occurs within God’s sovereign orchestration of events.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 40:14 and 40:16 teach about discernment and leadership in the post-exilic community?
options: Leaders must exercise discernment and avoid false accusations to maintain peace
All accusations against leaders should be accepted without question
Leadership is irrelevant in times of crisis
Suspicion and mistrust are the foundation of community
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders must exercise discernment and avoid false accusations to maintain peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:14 reveals suspicion of Ishmael's plot, but 40:16 shows Gedaliah’s refusal to believe false accusations, emphasizing wise leadership.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 40:1-6 teaches that God's judgment is arbitrary and unjust because Jeremiah is released while others are captive. What does Jeremiah 40:1-6 actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is just but includes mercy and specific purposes for individuals
God shows favoritism without reason, judging some unfairly
All captives are equally judged and condemned without distinction
Jeremiah’s release is due to human bribery, not God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is just but includes mercy and specific purposes for individuals
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:1-6 shows Jeremiah’s release according to God’s word, indicating His justice balanced with mercy and purpose for Jeremiah’s continued mission.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 40:7 teach about the role of leadership over God’s people during exile?
options: God appoints leaders even in exile to care for the remnant
Leadership is unnecessary once exile begins
Only prophets can lead God’s people, not secular leaders
The people must lead themselves without appointed authority
questions.correctAnswer: God appoints leaders even in exile to care for the remnant
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:7 explains that Gedaliah was made governor over those left in the land, showing God’s provision of leadership during exile.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 40:9 specifically demonstrate in Gedaliah’s oath to the captains and their men?
options: Faithfulness
Wrath
Jealousy
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 40:9, Gedaliah swears to the captains to serve the king of Babylon and promises wellbeing, reflecting God’s faithfulness through his appointed governor.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 40:11-12 connect to the broader biblical theme of gathering and restoration?
options: It prefigures the eventual return of the dispersed people to their land as part of God's redemptive plan
It shows permanent scattering without hope of return
It denies any future restoration for the exiles
It emphasizes total destruction without any remnant
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the eventual return of the dispersed people to their land as part of God's redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:11-12 records Jews returning from various countries to Judah, foreshadowing God's promise of restoration and regathering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 40:6 and 40:12 teach about God's providential preservation of His people?
options: God preserves a faithful remnant who return and dwell in the land
God abandons His people completely after judgment
Human effort alone restores the people without divine aid
God’s preservation excludes any future return from exile
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a faithful remnant who return and dwell in the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:6 shows Jeremiah dwelling with the remnant, and 40:12 shows Jews returning, indicating God's providential preservation of His people.
